speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition, can you tell me exactly when the weakness and decreased sensation in your right arm started?

speaker: Patient
text: 55-year-old male bodybuilder. The patient has been experiencing weakness in his right arm for a few weeks, which has progressively worsened to the point of dropping objects. He also reports a recent unexplained weight loss of 17 pounds and has a history of diabetes. The patient admits to chronic alcohol use, heavy smoking, and anabolic steroid use.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the weight loss and steroid use, I need to rule out malignancy or spinal cord compression. Do you have any neck pain, numbness in your legs, or changes in your bowel or bladder control?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Weakness in the right arm. I also have Decreased sensation in the right arm, Dull aching and burning pain in the right arm, Significant weight loss.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you experience any pain or numbness radiating down your arm to your fingers, and is the weakness present in all muscles of the arm or specific ones? REQUEST TEST: MRI Cervical Spine

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the cervical spine MRI is normal, I need to rule out a peripheral nerve issue or a central lesion. Do you have any weakness or sensory changes in your legs, face, or the left arm? REQUEST TEST: Brain_MRI

speaker: Doctor
text: With normal brain and cervical spine imaging, I must consider metabolic or systemic causes like paraneoplastic syndromes given your significant weight loss and steroid history.
